# Configure Okta as the SCIM identity provider

This topic describes how to create a custom Okta application and configure SCIM provisioning for HCP Terraform.

@include 'beta.mdx'

## Overview

Complete the following steps to configure Okta for SCIM provisioning:

1. Create a custom application in Okta with SAML SSO.
1. Enable SCIM in HCP Terraform and generate a SCIM token.
1. Configure the SCIM connection in Okta.
1. Enable provisioning actions in Okta.
1. Assign users and configure group push.
1. Verify synchronization.

## Prerequisites

Before configuring SCIM provisioning with Okta, verify the following:

- Your HCP Terraform organization is on a paid plan (Essentials, Standard, or Premium).
- You have administrator access to your Okta instance. Contact the Okta support team if you are unsure whether your Okta product supports SCIM.
- You are using SAML SSO (not HCP SSO) for your HCP Terraform organization.
- You have reviewed [Set up SCIM provisioning](/terraform/cloud-docs/users-teams-organizations/scim/configure) and completed the preparation steps.

## Create a custom application in Okta

During the Beta, you cannot use the existing Terraform Cloud OIN gallery application because it does not support enabling SCIM. You must create a custom application.

1. From your Okta Admin Dashboard, navigate to **Applications** > **Applications**.
1. Click **Create App Integration**.
1. Select **SAML 2.0** and click **Next**.
1. Name the application. Use a descriptive name such as `Terraform Cloud – Beta`. You may also include additional information such as the environment or organization name.
1. Click **Next**.
1. Under **Configure SAML**, set the following values. The SSO URL and Audience URI are temporary values that you replace in a later step:
   - **Single sign-on URL**: `https://app.terraform.io/sso/saml/placeholder`
   - **Audience URI (SP Entity ID)**: `placeholder`
   - **Name ID format**: `EmailAddress`
   - **Application username**: `Okta username`
   - **Update application username on**: `Create and update`
1. Under **Feedback**, select **This is an internal app that we have created**.
1. Click **Finish**.
1. Copy the **Metadata URL** to use in the HCP Terraform SSO configuration.
1. Follow the SSO configuration steps in [Use single sign-on with Okta for HCP Terraform](/terraform/cloud-docs/users-teams-organizations/single-sign-on/okta), up to and including enabling SSO.
1. In the Okta application, update the following with the values from the HCP Terraform SSO configuration:
   - **Single sign-on URL**: Replace with the **Assertion Consumer URL** from HCP Terraform.
   - **Audience URI (SP Entity ID)**: Replace with the **Entity ID (Audience)** from HCP Terraform.
1. Verify the SSO configuration by clicking **Test**. If the test succeeds, click **Enable**.

## Enable SCIM in HCP Terraform

Enable SCIM provisioning in HCP Terraform to obtain the credentials for Okta configuration.

1. Log in to HCP Terraform and navigate to your organization.
1. Click **Organization settings** and then **SCIM provisioning**.
1. Click **Enable SCIM**.
1. Click **Generate SCIM token**.
1. Set an expiration date between 30 days and 1 year from the creation date.
1. Copy and save the SCIM token. Store it securely.
1. Copy and save the URL from the **Base URL** field.

## Configure the SCIM connection in Okta

After SCIM is enabled in HCP Terraform, configure the SCIM connection in your Okta application.

1. Sign in to the Okta Admin Console.
1. Navigate to **Applications** and open your custom HCP Terraform application.
1. On the **General** tab under **App Settings**, click **Edit** and set **Provisioning** to **SCIM**. Click **Save**.
1. Click the **Provisioning** tab.
1. Click **Edit** for the **SCIM Connection** and complete the following:
   - **SCIM connector base URL**: Enter the Base URL you copied from HCP Terraform.
   - **Unique identifier field for users**: Set to `email`.
   - **Supported provisioning actions**: Select **Push New Users**, **Push Profile Updates**, and **Push Groups**.
   - **Authentication Mode**: Select **HTTP Header**.
   - **Authorization**: Enter the SCIM token you copied from HCP Terraform.
1. Click **Test Connector Configuration** to verify the connection.
1. Click **Save**.

## Enable provisioning actions

After the SCIM connection is verified, new settings appear under the **Provisioning** tab.

1. Click **To App** and click **Edit**.
1. Select the **Enable** checkbox for each of the following options:
   - **Create Users**
   - **Update User Attributes**
   - **Deactivate Users**
1. Click **Save**.

## Assign users and configure group push

### Assign users

1. Click the **Assignments** tab and click **Assign**.
1. Select the users or groups you want to provision and click **Assign**.

HCP Terraform creates and updates assigned users through your IdP.

### Configure group push

To synchronize Okta groups as HCP Terraform teams:

1. Click the **Push Groups** tab.
1. Click **Push Groups** to select groups to provision.
1. Search for and select the groups you want to synchronize.
1. Click **Save**.

HCP Terraform creates a team for each pushed group when the group is synchronized. IdP group names become team names in HCP Terraform.

## Validate the configuration

After configuration, verify that provisioning works correctly.

### Verify user provisioning

1. Assign a test user in Okta.
1. Check that the user appears in HCP Terraform within 5 minutes.
1. Navigate to **Organization settings** > **Users** and verify the user status shows **Synced - Provisioned**.
1. Test that the user can log in using SSO.

### Verify group provisioning

1. Push a test group from Okta.
1. Navigate to **Organization settings** > **Teams** and verify the group appears as a team.
1. Confirm team membership reflects the group membership in Okta.

## Troubleshooting

### Test Connector Configuration fails

- Verify the SCIM Base URL is correct.
- Verify the SCIM token has not expired. Generate a new token in HCP Terraform if needed.

### Users not provisioned

- Verify the user is assigned to the HCP Terraform application in Okta.
- Verify the **Create Users** provisioning action is enabled.
- Check the Okta provisioning logs for errors.

### Duplicate users created

- Verify the primary email in Okta matches the HCP Terraform account email exactly.
- Delete duplicate users and re-sync.

### Synchronization not working

- Check the token expiration date in HCP Terraform.
- Test the connector configuration in Okta.
- Check Okta provisioning logs for errors.

For additional troubleshooting, refer to [Troubleshoot SCIM provisioning](/terraform/cloud-docs/users-teams-organizations/scim/troubleshooting).
